plan.title: bug(lifecycle): verify:orphan-active prefers a stale cached issue state over the live read that would correct it

narratives.Description: bug(lifecycle): verify:orphan-active prefers a stale cached issue state over the live read that would correct it
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`verify:orphan-active` prefers a **stale cached issue state over the live read that would correct it**. A cache hit is returned unconditionally, with no age bound and no basis reporting, so the gate can be confidently wrong — and being wrong is exactly what stops it from checking.

Recut after an N=3 design-critique panel (successor lean 5427870380). The panel broke the original framing unanimously. Two claims in the first version were false and are withdrawn below.

## Withdrawn: "there is no live fallback"

The original body quoted `readCachedIssueState` in isolation and concluded a cache miss returns `null` and passes vacuously. **That is wrong.** The decision point is `resolveIssueState`:

```ts
const cached = readCachedIssueState(projectRoot, ref);
if (cached !== null) return cached;
if (skipGh) return null;
return fetchIssueStateLive(ref, runGh);
```

A miss already falls through to a live REST read, locked by a test named *"uses live gh issue state when cache is absent."* One critic reran that file 24/24 green; another measured a run with no `.deft-cache` at all and got a correct exit 1. **Vacuous green requires `--skip-gh`,** which is a deliberate flag rather than an accident of cache state.

Also withdrawn: the fresh-clone argument built on that claim.

## The actual defect

A **cache hit wins unconditionally**. No freshness bound, no age check, no comparison. A stale `open` beats reality and suppresses the live path.

Measured on 2026-08-26 immediately after #3611 closed:

| | |
|---|---|
| live state of #3611 | `closed` |
| `.deft-cache` entry | `open` |
| cache written | ~12 h earlier |
| `verify:orphan-active` | `scanned 1 running brief`, **exit 0** |

Reproduced again the same day during a session ceremony: `cache-fresh: stale-by-drift — 2 cached-open issue(s) absent from live open set`. Same cache, different consumer, and that one noticed.

## Remedy: split by query shape

The panel converged here. **Not one mechanism — two.**

**Scoped `--issue N`** — a direct authoritative read. It is a proof obligation before DONE, N is 1, and it should stay fail-closed on unknown. Largely already correct today.

**Unscoped aggregate** — one complete, fail-closed open-issue inventory. This is exactly what #3752 shipped, measured at **4.2 s constant**, against a per-brief crossover of roughly 5 briefs on `gh` and 1 on `ghx`. Per-brief live reads are the mechanism #3752 *removed*; reintroducing them here would repeat it at lower-but-policy-reachable N.

### Why per-brief live reads were rejected

Measured occupancy of `active/` across 295 snapshots since 2026-07-01: **median 1 running brief, p75 2, p90 4, p95 6, maximum 9.** So the ordinary case is genuinely cheap.

But the swarm WIP cap is 20, and at that ceiling sequential reads measured **14.2 s** on one host and **76.6 s** on another with the default binary — in a gate that sits in the **fast-preflight tier**, where wall clock rather than quota is the constraint. A plausible upper bound of 400 requests exists if 20 cohort workers each check 20 briefs; that amplification is **unverified**.

### "Live" is itself a cache

`defaultRunGh` resolves through `resolveBinary()`, which prefers **`ghx` — a cached GET proxy**. So no live-read remedy can honestly promise "regardless of `.deft-cache` contents or age", because the call may be served from a second cache this gate never inspects. Either bypass `ghx` here or state that the guarantee is bounded by the proxy.

### One trap for the implementer

`probeCacheDrift` already builds a live open-number inventory, but its helper **defaults to a 1,000-item limit**. Reusing that capped set as a closed-state oracle would misclassify open issue 1001+ in a larger repository. The inventory must be complete and fail closed on truncation.

## Unknown is already bimodal — do not flatten it

Scoped `--issue N` turns unknown into an `unresolved` failure; the unscoped aggregate returns PASS on the first unknown. **Both are locked by tests.**

That is not an accident to fix with one rule. Scoped is a proof obligation before DONE. Aggregate must not make offline work network-authorized. "Fail closed on unknown" as a single undifferentiated rule would break offline use with active briefs; returning a clean sentence on an unavailable lookup launders absence into evidence. The contract must name which callers require proof.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A cache hit is not returned unconditionally — either bounded by age, or re-validated, with the choice recorded
- [ ] A tracked running brief whose issue is closed is detected regardless of `.deft-cache` contents or age, within the stated `ghx` caveat
- [ ] Unscoped aggregate resolves state via one complete, fail-closed open-issue inventory, not per-brief reads
- [ ] The inventory is complete: no truncation ambiguity, PR rows excluded, fail closed on command failure, malformed pages, pagination exhaustion, and buffer exhaustion
- [ ] Scoped `--issue N` keeps its authoritative read and stays fail-closed on unknown
- [ ] Output reports the **basis** of each verdict — cache or live, and cache age where cache was used — so a pass is distinguishable from an unverified pass
- [ ] Separate latency budgets are recorded for scoped and aggregate modes. None exist today, which is why "affordable" was unfalsifiable
- [ ] No regression: a running brief with an open issue still passes
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry

## Out of scope

- **The offline crash** — with neither `gh` nor `ghx` on PATH the gate throws an uncaught `ScmStubError` and exits 1, which the documented three-state contract reads as *"orphan found."* An absent toolchain reported as a lifecycle violation. Filed separately.
- Preventing in-flight briefs from being committed. That framing was itself refuted on #3766; active briefs are tracked here by design.
- The `cache_fresh` forge-error fail-open decided on #3738.

## Environment

Measured at `0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5` and later, Windows 11, `@deftai/directive` 0.107.0.

Related: #3429 (the gate's contract), #3476, #3752 (the open-inventory mechanism this reuses), #3738 (adjacent cache-trust pattern), #3156.

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-26T15:22:35Z)

model: claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast
role: triage

## Triage

mechanism-shaped: true

design-critique: warranted, because this changes what a fail-closed lifecycle gate promises, and the remedy set is four unresolved directions with different safety properties. #3156 applies directly: altering when a gate answers, and on what basis, is not a thing to do quietly.

refutation-target: the gate only inspects briefs already in `active/`, a handful at a time, so a live REST read per running brief is affordable and is the right replacement for the cache read.

## Non-self-arbitration disclosure

I filed this issue and I am running its triage. I may not clear my own claims. The refutation target above is my own preferred direction, named deliberately because it is the one I would most regret being wrong about.

There is a second reason to attack it hard. **I used this gate's exit-0 as evidence in my own verification claims** — several times overnight I reported a tree as clean on the strength of `verify:orphan-active` passing. If the gate's verdict is cache-conditioned, those claims were softer than I stated them. So a critic here is auditing my evidence standard, not only the code.

## Confirmed live while triaging

The staleness is not theoretical. Attempting a session ceremony minutes ago:

```
deft cache-fresh: stale-by-drift -- 2 cached-open issue(s) absent from live open set (deftai/directive).
```

Two issues closed overnight were still cached as open. That is the same cache the gate reads. A forced `cache:fetch-all` cleared it.

## Audit markers

- `audit:cost` — the affordability claim is unmeasured. "A handful of active briefs" is an impression. Measure the actual distribution, including the worst case, before accepting that a live read per brief is cheap. Note the adjacent precedent runs the other way: #3752 was filed precisely because a per-anchor live read did not scale.
- `audit:absent-cache` — I claim a fresh clone has no `.deft-cache`, so every lookup returns `null` and the gate is vacuously green. Verify rather than assume; there may be a bootstrap path that populates it.
- `audit:failclosed-boundary` — "fail closed on unknown" sounds obviously right and may not be. A gate that hard-fails whenever the cache is cold would fail on every fresh clone and every offline run. Establish what unknown should actually do before adopting it.

## What is solid

The mechanism is directly cited and simple: `readCachedIssueState` builds a path under `.deft-cache`, returns `null` when the file is absent, and never consults live state or checks age. The measured instance is unambiguous — live `closed`, cached `open`, cache written roughly 12 hours earlier, gate exit 0 while scanning the brief in question.

## What the critique should press on

Beyond the target: whether this should be fixed in the gate at all, or whether the defect belongs to the cache layer — a gate reading a cache that nothing guarantees fresh may be the wrong place to intervene. If `cache_fresh` already exists as a separate gate that detects exactly this drift, the composition question is why one gate detects staleness while another silently consumes it.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-26T15:39:41Z)

model: cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast
role: critic

SHA `0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5`. Ceiling `5427447462` (inclusive). Charter: refutation. Fresh critic. All `file:line` cites re-opened at that SHA.

Refutation target: the gate only inspects briefs already in `active/`, a handful at a time, so a live REST read per running brief is affordable and is the right replacement for the cache read.

The conjunction does not survive. Affordability at observed N mostly does. "Right replacement" does not.

## The hole is a stale open hit, not a missing live path

class: `blocks-the-design`

Evidence: `resolveIssueState` at `packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts:153-167` returns a cache hit immediately and only then falls through to `fetchIssueStateLive` (`:129-151`). `readCachedIssueState` (`:98-127`) returns `null` on a missing file; that miss is not treated as `open`. The test `"uses live gh issue state when cache is absent"` (`evaluate.test.ts:571-590`) already locks the miss path. CLI `skipGh` defaults false (`packages/cli/src/verify-orphan-active.ts:31`). The body's sentence "there is no freshness check and no live fallback" is false for the second half. Re-verified at this SHA. The measured #3611 12h-stale-open instance is unverified here (cache for #3611 is now `closed`, `fetched_at=2026-08-26T15:20:49Z`); the code path that would honour a stale `open` hit without a live read is verified.

Concrete failure mode: binding direction 3 as "replace the cache read with live" repairs the wrong branch. The false green is `cached === "open"` suppressing live, not `cached === null`. A patch that only adds live-on-miss is a no-op. A patch that deletes the cache read pays REST on every check even when the cache is one minute old and closed (safe).

Disposition consequence: do not bind "no live fallback" or "replace the cache read". Bind: cached `open` is not evidence; cached `closed` is. That is already written in the sibling land gate.

## Per-brief live is not the right replacement

class: `blocks-the-design`

Evidence: three existing mechanisms already do the live work this direction proposes, without making `verify:orphan-active` a sequential per-issue client.

1. `verify:completed-tracked` `defaultResolveIssueState` (`packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:207-231`) trusts cached `closed`, ignores cached `open` as proof, and revalidates via live when `skipGh` is false. Test: `"revalidates stale open cache via live gh when skipGh is false (#3264 P1)"` (`completed-tracked-on-delivery.test.ts:385-406`). Same `readCachedIssueState` shape, opposite open-hit policy.
2. `verify:cache-fresh` sits immediately before `verify:orphan-active` on both check lists (`packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts:85-86` and `:133-135`). Its drift probe (`packages/core/src/cache/fetch.ts:871-902`) lists live open numbers and flags cached-open issues absent from that set — the exact #3611 shape. The triage write-back already saw `stale-by-drift -- 2 cached-open issue(s) absent from live open set`. On the `task check` path the previous gate can already fail this tree when the probe succeeds. `runDriftProbe` still fail-opens on throw (`preflight-cache/evaluate.ts:358-377`, #3738); that is why composition is not sufficient alone.
3. #3752 shipped `restIssueListOpenInventory` (`packages/core/src/scm/gh-rest.ts:526-584`): one paginated open-only subprocess; absence from a complete inventory is non-open. That is the adjacent precedent's actual remedy, not "stop doing live reads". A per-brief `gh api repos/.../issues/N` loop is the shape #3752 removed from release Step 3.

PR state is already live on every unscoped scan (`fetchPrMerged`, `evaluate.ts:169-188`, `:258-266`). Issue state is the only cache-first path.

Concrete failure mode: binding a sequential live GET per running brief as the replacement duplicates (2) on the check path, ignores (1) as the already-reviewed open-hit policy, and reintroduces the #3752 sequential-per-anchor shape on a hot path (`task check` / pre-commit / pre-push) even though N is small. #3156 applies: this issue is a named gate-definition change, which is the legitimate path; the wrong change is still a gate change.

Disposition consequence: the target cannot bind as the preferred remedy. Lift (1) into issue-state resolution (shared helper), and/or ask unscoped scans to consume a fail-closed open inventory from (3). Keep live GET for `--issue N` if the DONE path must not depend on cache-fresh having just run.

Road not taken: blanket live-always (smallest patch, closes the stale hit). Rejected because it ignores (1)–(3) and pays REST when cached `closed` is already fail-closed evidence. Steelmans of the target: at N=1 the extra GET is ~750 ms and the DONE path is exactly one origin. What would flip this finding back to "right replacement": if (1) could not be lifted without dragging the completed-tracked corpus scan, if (2) were not on the same check list, and if (3) did not exist.

## audit:cost — affordable at observed N; that does not select the remedy

class: `sharpens-framing`

Evidence, methods named:

- Dispatch SHA `0a82ac96` `xbrief/active/` tree: empty (git `ls-tree 0a82ac96:xbrief/active` missing). 31 first-parent `origin/master` samples spanning 2026-07-01..2026-08-26, every 10th of 295 commits that touched the path: all 0 files. Sample min=max=0.
- Issue measurement SHA `8f5dd900`: 1 file, `plan.status=running`, issue #3611. Matches the body's "scanned 1 running brief".
- Working tree now: 2 untracked running briefs (#3599 refs #3599+#3433; #3611 refs #3611).
- `git log --all --shortstat -- xbrief/active` (first 80 commits shown): every commit is `1 file changed`. Track one, untrack one. No swarm-sized committed `active/` set in that window.
- `plan.policy.wipCap` is unset on this repo's PROJECT-DEFINITION; `DEFAULT_WIP_CAP = 20` (`packages/core/src/policy/wip.ts:13`). WIP counts `pending/`+`active/` (`:16`, `:81`). Plausible worst case for a mid-flight cohort is 20 running briefs if they are all committed into one tree. Observed committed max in the measured window: 1. Full 924-ref scan unverified (`ls-tree` here ~3.5–7 s per SHA).
- Live GET cost on this machine, `gh api repos/deftai/directive/issues/N`: 788 ms / 751 ms / 717 ms for #3611, #3767, #3429. PR #3763: 930 ms. `core` remaining 4994/5000 after those calls. Sequential 20 issue GETs ≈ 15 s unverified as a wall measurement (extrapolated). #3752's 1,156-call / 38 min figure is history-scaled release Step 3, not this gate.

Concrete failure mode: stating "a handful, so live per brief is cheap" is true for the trees this gate actually sees on master (0) and for the incident (1) and for `--issue N` (1). It is not a measurement of a swarm worktree that inherited a full WIP set, and it does not follow that per-brief GET is the right live shape. #3752 cut the other way on scale (1,156 vs 20) and on shape (sequential per-anchor vs one inventory). Both matter. The exception for `active/` holds on scale. It does not hold as a reason to skip the inventory already shipped.

Disposition consequence: record N as WIP-capped and empirically 0–2 on this repo, not "unmeasured handful". Do not use cost to select direction 3. A 15 s pre-commit tax at cap=20 is affordable relative to 38 min and still the worse live design when (3) exists.

## audit:absent-cache — a fresh clone is not vacuously green when gh works

class: `sharpens-framing`

Evidence: `.deft-cache/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:74`). `verify:orphan-active` does not call `maybeAutoPopulateEmptyCache` (`packages/core/src/cache/empty-populate.ts:52-54`); that bootstrap is on `verify:cache-fresh` (`preflight-cache/evaluate.ts:414-423`). `session:start` skips hydrate on the default hot path (`session-start.ts:1636`, #2991). This repo's `task verify:cache-fresh` bakes `--allow-missing-bootstrap` (`tasks/verify.yml:319`; also `framework-commands.ts:108` and ritual entrypoint `:127-133`), so a missing cache does not fail `task check` here. After that, orphan-active with default `skipGh=false` live-fetches. Unscoped unknown still `return PASS` (`evaluate.ts:272-276`); the test `"does not orphan when issue state is unknown"` (`evaluate.test.ts:495-508`) locks that fail-open. Scoped `--issue N` fail-closes on unknown (`evaluate.ts:236-238`; test `:365-384`).

Concrete failure mode: the body's "fresh clone has no `.deft-cache`, so every lookup returns `null` and the gate is vacuously green" names the wrong mechanism. Vacuous green is unscoped + (`skipGh` or live failure), not absent cache per se. A cold clone with working `gh` already takes the live path. A cold clone with `--allow-missing-bootstrap` on cache-fresh still reaches that path. Offline / `--skip-gh` / live 429 is the actual silent pass, and it is intentional in the unscoped tests.

Disposition consequence: drop "absent cache ⇒ pass" as an AC. Split: (a) cache miss + live ok already works; (b) unscoped unknown remains fail-open; (c) `--issue N` unknown already fail-closes. Bootstrap that exists is cache-fresh empty-populate and `triage:bootstrap`, not this gate.

## audit:failclosed-boundary — unknown is already split; do not unify on fail-closed

class: `blocks-the-design`

Evidence: the two call sites already disagree, on purpose. Unscoped `task check` / pre-push: unknown ⇒ PASS (`evaluate.ts:272-276`). After-merge `--issue N`: unknown ⇒ `unresolved`, exit 1, retry remediation, not `scope:complete` (`:236-238`, `:329-338`). The sibling land gate documents the same split (`completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:635-644`, #3478): unscoped keeps an offline allowance; named `--issue` must not exit 0 on an uncached origin. `--skip-gh` is a public flag (`tasks/verify.yml:506`). Hard-fail on unknown for the unscoped path fails every `--skip-gh` fixture, every offline `task check`, and every live-miss after `--allow-missing-bootstrap` let a fresh clone through.

Concrete failure mode: direction 1 as "fail closed on unknown" without naming the call site inverts the unscoped gate into a connectivity check. Agents then "fix" red by `--skip-gh` or by deleting the brief, which is the #3156-adjacent failure: the gate goes red for not knowing, not for a shipped residue. The DONE-path evidence hole is the opposite polarity: `--issue N` must not treat stale cached `open` as known.

Disposition consequence: do not bind a single unknown policy. Keep unscoped unknown as fail-open (or as an explicit `unverified` line that still exits 0). Keep `--issue N` fail-closed on unknown. Change the open-hit policy, not the miss policy. Output-the-basis (direction 4) can bind on both sites without changing exit codes.

## Injection / swarm lens

class: `footnote`

The target touches shared cache state, worktrees, and concurrent `gh` identity. `.deft-cache/` is per-worktree and gitignored, so a `git worktree add` clone is cache-cold. Live-on-miss already fires there. Blanket live-on-hit would multiply sequential GETs across N workers sharing one REST `core` bucket. No prompt/envelope/untrusted-input change. Occupancy lease not involved. No A2A.

## Evidence standard (interested-party exit-0)

class: `footnote`

I did not rerun `verify:orphan-active` against the 12h-stale-open cache; that file is gone. I did re-read the code the exit-0 claim depends on: an `open` cache hit never reaches live. A DONE-path `--issue N` against that hit exits 0. `verify:completed-tracked` is not on `task check` and would still revalidate live if it were run. An exit-0 from this gate alone is not proof the origin is open.

What would have broken the refutation of "right replacement": no live-on-miss path, no sibling revalidate-open, cache-fresh not earlier in the same check list, and no `restIssueListOpenInventory`. Affordability at N≤2 would have survived anyway.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-26T15:43:29Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol-medium
role: critic

**Verdict:** The refutation target does not survive as a general design. Direct live REST is affordable for the observed normal case and is correct for the one-origin `--issue N` proof path. It is not the right aggregate replacement at the swarm bound.

## Cache miss already goes live

class: `blocks-the-design`
audit: `absent-cache` — resolved

**Evidence.** At dispatch SHA `0a82ac96`, `resolveIssueState` reads cache first but calls live REST whenever the entry is absent; only an explicit `--skip-gh` suppresses that fallback ([evaluate.ts L98-L167](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts#L98-L167)). The repository already has a cache-absent/live-fallback test ([evaluate.test.ts L571-L590](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.test.ts#L571-L590)); I reran the file: 24/24 tests passed. A fresh framework checkout can remain cache-empty because cache-fresh explicitly accepts bootstrap state ([preflight-cache/evaluate.ts L411-L460](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/preflight-cache/evaluate.ts#L411-L460)), but that does not make orphan-active return `null` while GitHub is reachable.

**Concrete failure mode.** A change described as adding live fallback would preserve the actual defect: a stale cached `open` is returned before live REST is attempted. The issue body claim “There is no ... live fallback” and the fresh-clone/vacuous-green mechanism conflate stale-cache preference with cache absence. Cache absence is silently green only when live lookup also fails or `--skip-gh` is set.

**Disposition consequence.** Recut the mechanism and acceptance around stale cached state taking precedence, plus unknown-state reporting. Do not bind a design whose primary cache-miss remedy is already implemented.

## Normal is small; swarm scale is not free

class: `blocks-the-design`
audit: `cost` — resolved

**Evidence and method.** I replayed 295 first-parent snapshots that changed `xbrief/active/` from 2026-07-01 through the dispatch SHA, parsed the actual `plan.status`, and counted running briefs. This is transition-sampled, not time-weighted: median 1, p75 2, p90 4, p95 6, maximum 9 (frequency: 0=89, 1=103, 2=35, 3=25, 4=16, 5=10, 6=5, 7=5, 8=4, 9=3). The maximum issue-reference count in one snapshot was 13; one brief carried as many as 8 GitHub refs. Ten sequential live issue reads on this host took 7.110 s (0.711 s/read). A complete open inventory returned 560 issues in 4.174 s. The normal historical case is therefore cheap; #3752 at 1,156 anchors is not comparable to median 1 or maximum 9.

The documented swarm policy can fill `pending/ + active/` to a default WIP cap of 20 ([core-phase-0.md L64-L70, L88-L114](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md#L64-L114)). At the measured mean, 20 sequential reads extrapolate to 14.22 s per aggregate gate run. If 20 cohort workers each see and check all 20 active briefs, that is 400 REST requests and about 284 aggregate worker-seconds per check wave; whether every worktree carries the full activated cohort is **unverified**, so treat 400 as a plausible upper-bound scenario, not an observed count.

**Concrete failure mode.** A per-brief subprocess loop makes aggregate check latency and REST load scale with cohort size and multiplies under concurrent workers. It repeats the mechanism class that #3752 removed, at a lower but policy-reachable N.

**Disposition consequence.** “Affordable” survives for ordinary observed occupancy because no gate budget was supplied; a budget below roughly 14 s at cap, or confirmed N-by-N worker amplification, would break it outright. “Right replacement” does not survive universally. Record separate budgets for scoped and aggregate modes.

## Unknown is a proof-mode boundary

class: `sharpens-framing`
audit: `failclosed-boundary` — resolved

**Evidence.** The code already distinguishes modes. `--issue N` turns unknown issue or PR state into an `unresolved` failure ([evaluate.ts L214-L255](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts#L214-L255)); the unscoped aggregate returns PASS on the first unknown issue ([evaluate.ts L258-L287](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts#L258-L287)). Tests lock both outcomes ([evaluate.test.ts L365-L410, L495-L508](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.test.ts#L365-L508)). Both framework and consumer aggregate check lists run cache-fresh before orphan-active ([gate-lists.ts L79-L86, L128-L135](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts#L79-L135)), but standalone orphan-active is also used as after-merge evidence.

**Concrete failure mode.** Hard-failing every aggregate unknown makes offline work with active briefs network-authorized. Returning exit 0 with a clean sentence launders an unavailable lookup into evidence, which is the failure already disclosed on this issue.

**Disposition consequence.** Keep scoped `--issue N` fail-closed on unknown: it is a proof obligation before DONE. For aggregate/offline use, an explicit unverified or operator-bypass state may permit local continuation, but it must not emit or be cited as a verified-clean result. The contract must name which callers require proof; “fail closed on unknown” cannot be one undifferentiated rule.

## Split the mechanism by query shape

class: `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** An existing mechanism already builds a live open-number inventory: `probeCacheDrift` compares cached-open entries to `listOpenIssueNumbers` ([cache/fetch.ts L870-L905](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/0a82ac9665880210b4b7da3c0e841733ad927ea5/packages/core/src/cache/fetch.ts#L870-L905)). Quota is not the constraint at any of these sizes. The affordability claim needs an N and a binary or it should not be written down.

**`audit:absent-cache` -- resolved, refuted.** The premise is right about the file and wrong about the consequence. A fresh clone has no `.deft-cache`, `readCachedIssueState` does return `null`, and the gate then reads live and correctly fails (measured: exit 1 on closed #3611 with no cache present). The vacuous-green case is real but narrow -- it requires `--skip-gh` on the unscoped path, or an unreachable forge. There is also a bootstrap path (`deft triage:bootstrap`, named in cache-fresh's own recovery hint, `preflight-cache/evaluate.ts:335-337`), so the fresh-clone state is transient by design. Acceptance criterion 2 is already met on the default path; retarget it at `--skip-gh` and at the unscoped unknown branch.

**`audit:failclosed-boundary` -- resolved, adverse to the simple form.** Covered in finding 3. The gate already implements two unknown policies, and the codebase's implicit answer is the right one: fail closed where a worker is asserting DONE about a named origin, report unverified where the gate is sweeping. A global fail-closed rule breaks every offline and gh-less run. The urgent defect is not the policy but the crash: a missing SCM binary currently produces an uncaught `ScmStubError` at exit 1, which the three-state contract reads as "orphan found". Fix that first; it is unambiguous, it is cheap, and it does not depend on which cache direction wins.

---

## Road not taken, and the steelman

There were three plausible mechanisms, not two: per-brief live read, one fail-closed open inventory per run, and leaving state resolution alone while adding an age bound plus a printed basis (directions 2 and 4 in the body, which nobody is arguing for). I rejected the third as the whole answer -- an age bound cannot decide the `--issue N` DONE case, where the question is about one specific origin at one specific moment and a two-hour-old cache entry is not evidence. But it is the cheapest correct fix for the sweep, and pairing it with a live read only for the scoped path is the shape I would defend: the DONE path is where the guarantee is needed and where N is 1.

**Steelman of the target.** At the measured p50 of one running brief with one issue reference, a `gh` read costs about 0.8 s, is unconditionally correct, needs no completeness contract, and cannot invert the gate the way a truncated inventory can. Inventory-based reasoning fails toward "closed", and "closed" is the direction that tells an operator to run `scope:complete` on live work. Preferring N cheap correct reads over one call with a subtle completeness obligation is a real safety argument, and at N=1 it wins outright.

**What flips it.** Volume and binary. The argument holds while N stays near the median and the binary is `gh`. It fails at the cap, and it fails immediately under `ghx`, which is what the framework actually prefers.

**What would have saved the target.** If `resolveBinary` pinned `gh` for this call path, if `active/` were bounded well below the `wipCap` ceiling by something other than convention, and if #3752 had not already landed a one-call inventory for this exact predicate, the target would have survived on cost and been the right mechanism. Two of those three are fixable in the same change.

---

**`footnote` -- the evidence standard, not the verdicts.** The disclosure asks whether overnight "tree is clean" claims resting on this gate's exit 0 were softer than stated. They were unattributable rather than wrong. An exit 0 produced by a live read is sound; an exit 0 produced by a cache hit is only as sound as the entry; an exit 0 produced by a brief with unrecognized reference types (finding 6) verified nothing at all. The output distinguishes none of these, so no past exit 0 can be classified after the fact. That is the strongest available statement, and it is an argument for acceptance criterion 3 being the load-bearing one rather than criterion 1.

**`footnote` -- gate integrity (#3156).** This change alters when a fail-closed gate answers and on what basis, so it is a gate-definition change and belongs on the issue-to-PR path, which is where it is. Worth naming explicitly: any criterion that turns unknown into exit 0 with an `unverified` line is a *weakening* of the current scoped behaviour, and #3156 requires that be stated as the change rather than arriving as a side effect of a cache refactor.

**`footnote` -- ceiling hygiene.** A single bulk `issues/3767/comments` fetch returned one comment above the stated id ceiling.
